It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of a world that seeks to “remodel the way we think about truth” through the halls of human reason, and I must ask you with a gentle spirit: why do you ask after the nature of idolatry in scientific institutions and the temptation of knowledge in this hour? [1, 1315, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the “fortresses of ideology” that are “set against truth and God” in modern academia, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul against a “spirit of fraud” that suggests human discovery can ever replace divine revelation? [43, 1406, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to offer “spiritual placebos” or suggest that “logic is ruled by pride,” we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” by demanding that we “examine everything carefully” within the claims of men [11, 28, 43, 116, 1344, 1503, 1515, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the arrogance of human knowledge is not an “administrative anomaly” but evidence of a “radically depraved” heart that is a “perpetual factory of idols” [11, 15, 68, 191, 1143, 1316, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Folly of Professional Wisdom (Romans 1:21–22)**

**Verse**
“Because, although they knew God, they did not glorify Him as God, nor were thankful, but became futile in their thoughts, and their foolish hearts were darkened. Professing to be wise, they became fools” (Romans 1:21–22). [1073, 1359, 1736, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The sources teach that “unbelief is the seed” of the opinion that truth is unknowable apart from human deduction, for “the carnal mind is enmity against God” (Romans 8:7) [1326, 1337, 1500, Conversation History]. When scientific institutions attempt to “define truth without reference to God,” they fall into the trap where “logic is ruled by pride” and “intellects are ruled by lust,” turning the “ability to think clearly”—which is a “tremendous blessing from God”—into a tool for “self-aggrandizement” [43, 102, 103, 1359, 1734, Conversation History]. The Reformed faith asserts that “God is the author, source, determiner, governor, arbiter, ultimate standard, and final judge of all truth,” and to suggest that human discovery “evolves and changes” while God’s truth is “soft and pliable” is to “profess to be wise” while becoming a “fool” [1355, 1364, 1371, 1373, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by a “big string of degrees” or “achievements, insights, and wisdom” that do not start with the Lord, for “if you’re going to boast, boast in this, that you know and understand Me” (Jeremiah 9:24) [834, 1406, 1502, Conversation History]. Recognize that “he who trusts in his own heart is a fool” and you must instead “tremble at My word” (Proverbs 28:26; Isaiah 66:2) [251, 1039, 1381, 1503, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Gentile context** of Rome, Paul was addressing those who could clearly see “His eternal power and Godhead” through “the things that are made,” yet chose to “suppress the truth in unrighteousness” (Romans 1:18, 20) [1073, 1357, 1736, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our view of this “natural revelation” by showing that it is sufficient to leave the world “without excuse,” yet only the “Spirit-inspired Scriptures” can “make you wise for salvation” (2 Timothy 3:15) [1341, 1358, 1461, 1532, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: The Temptation of Knowledge Without God (Genesis 3:5–6)**

**Verse**
“ ‘For God knows that in the day you eat of it your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.’ So when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree desirable to make one wise, she took of its fruit and ate. She also gave to her husband with her, and he ate” (Genesis 3:5–6). [962, 1272, 1286, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The “record of history” begins with the “savage spiritual conflict” of the Fall, where Satan’s “evil dialectic” first tempted humanity to “become like God” by seeking “special knowledge” apart from His command [1223, 1369, 1417, 1458, Conversation History]. Scientific pursuits become “idolatrous” when they are driven by the same “human pride” that built the Tower of Babel, seeking to “make a name for ourselves” rather than “ascribing greatness to our God” (Genesis 11:4; Deuteronomy 32:3) [860, 885, 1233, 1623, Conversation History]. The sources warn that “sin leads us to take shortcuts,” and when we seek to be “enlightened” by “cleverly devised myths” of human discovery while “ignoring the Word,” we are simply “wasting our lives in empty pursuits” [4, 298, 443, 1504, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You must “discipline your mind” to “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “worldly philosophies,” for “the Holy Spirit and the Spirit-inspired Scriptures” are given to “direct your steps” (Psalm 119:105) [51, 123, 1406, 1503, 1709, Conversation History]. “Trade in your worry for trust,” for the “kingdom of heaven is of such infinite value” that it far surpasses the “special treasures” of earthly discovery (Matthew 13:44) [27, 94, 201, 973, 1408, 1515, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual vs. Reality**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, “testifying in a dispute” required strict “safeguards” to ensure “justice for all,” protecting the community from “taking a bribe” for a false report (Exodus 23:8) [330, 367, 1072, 1230, 1317, 1365, 1473, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this by showing that our “witness” is to be “faithful and true,” and we must “refuse to yield submission” to any “spirit of error” that uses “scientific” language to “handle the word of God deceitfully” (2 Corinthians 4:2) [92, 1188, 1513, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: Exchanging the Truth for a Lie (Romans 1:25)**

**Verse**
“who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen” (Romans 1:25). [916, 934, 1359, 1664, 1737, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—echoed by **Voddie Baucham**—notes that “love can be sinful” when it is “directed at the wrong object,” such as when we “worship the creature” through a “coldhearted materialism” that “does not love God” [1719, 1721, 1733, 1737, 1740, Conversation History]. To “exchange the truth” is to participate in a “wholesale transformation” where “uncertainty is the new truth” and “doubt is canonized as humility,” which is actually “proud rebellion against divine revelation” [11, 1377, 1392, 1503, Conversation History]. This “spirit of fraud” allows the “god of this age” to “blind the minds of the unbelieving,” leading them to “establish their own righteousness” through their “scientific monuments” while remaining “dead in trespasses” (2 Corinthians 4:4; Romans 10:3) [102, 122, 214, 316, 1406, 1502, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” in “opinion polls” or “secular philosophy,” for “the Bible is the source of truth” and “His counsel shall stand” (Isaiah 46:10) [51, 101, 123, 1406, 1503, 1684, Conversation History]. Recognize that “your life is not your own” because you were “bought at a price,” and your “sole objective” is to “glorify God in your body” and your mind (1 Corinthians 6:20) [12, 101, 212, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
In the ancient **theocratic context**, God used “temporal signs” to “punish the fruit of the arrogant heart,” as seen when he “confused their language” at Babel [740, 1110, 1265, 1315, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” teaching that we “conquer” not through “carnal weaponry” or “intellectual status,” but “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony,” for “Jesus answered, ‘My kingdom is not of this world’ ” (John 18:36; Revelation 12:11) [13, 21, 32, 92, 1018, 1313, 1402, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 361, 405, 414, 444, 591, 834, 1138, 1450, Conversation History].

references.cited_text: As a Father Who Requires Obedience Because God was their Father, the people were required to obey Him. Deuteronomy 32:6 reiterates that: “Do you thus repay the LORD, O foolish and unwise people? Is not He your Father who has bought you?” The Biblical Perspective of God When Jesus arrived on the scene, He reintroduced His Jewish audience to God as a loving, beneficent Father to those who know, love, and obey Him. In the Sermon on the Mount, He taught them that the Father takes care of the needs of His children:

In light of that, it is significant that in both of these parables the main characters did precisely what most savvy investment advisors would strongly warn us against. The first man sold everything and bought one field. The second man sold everything and bought one pearl. Six Vital Truths About the Kingdom These two simple parables are not about principles of investment. They make a point that is spiritual: everything this world deems worthwhile or important counts as sheer loss compared to the surpassing value of knowing Christ and being part of His kingdom (Phil. 3:7–8). That one point summarizes several underlying lessons about the kingdom that are woven into these parables.
